name: How long does a bathtub-to-shower conversion take?

mainEntity.name: How long does a bathtub-to-shower conversion usually take in a real home, not just a one-day sales claim?
mainEntity.text: How long does a bathtub-to-shower conversion usually take in a real home, not just a one-day sales claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline depends on the scope of work. A basic direct replacement with prefabricated walls and no plumbing surprises may move quickly, while a custom tiled shower with drain changes, inspections, or structural repairs takes longer. In practice, homeowners should expect time for demolition, plumbing rough-in, waterproofing, curing or drying, wall installation, glass measurement, and final trim work. Delays are common when hidden moisture damage is found behind the old tub or when the contractor must wait for a permit inspection. In Los Angeles-area homes, older plumbing and uneven walls can also slow the project. The best way to get a reliable schedule is to ask the contractor for a milestone-based timeline, including what could extend the job. If the bathroom is the only shower in the house, planning for temporary access is essential. A realistic timeline is better than a fast promise that ignores inspections, materials lead times, and finishing details.
acceptedAnswer.description: A simple conversion can sometimes be finished in a few days, but real-world projects often take longer when plumbing, waterproofing, tile, or inspections are involved. If the layout changes, the job can stretch into one to two weeks or more depending on drying time and scope.
